cited.quote: Renovation work of temple cars, temple tanks and temple gardens in 100 temples

rationale: C3 mentions Rs.100 crore for renovating temple cars, tanks and gardens, a different object from consecration and festivities, and far below Rs.1000 crore. C5's Rs.1000 crore is for the urban improvement scheme (KNMT), not temples. No official step for this commitment.
No extract shows any request or resolution to the Union government on the OBC income ceiling. C4 concerns OBC reservation in a state law university, which is a different subject.

cited.quote: one shall belong to Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes and one shall be a woman

rationale: C1 and C2 describe trustee boards with reservation only for SC/ST and women. No extract shows any reservation for the Viswakarma community. C4 and C5 concern a public-services roster for MBC groups.

No extract shows a resolution or letter urging the Union to set up a National Commission for fishermen welfare. C4 urges the Union on release of fishermen in Sri Lankan custody, a different issue. C5 is a home guard recruitment order.

cited.quote: Women are economically empowered thorugh the Women Industrial Co-operative societies

rationale: C3 describes existing women industrial co-operative societies for poor, widowed and destitute women aged 18 to 40. C2/C5 sanction capital for labour-contract societies. None targets 12th-standard educated rural women as members, so no matching step.

cited.quote: hereby accord financial sanction for a sum of Rs.8.375 Crore
ESTABLISHMENT OF RURAL AGRICULTURE MARKET IN YEDAPALLI VILLAGE OF NILGIRIS DISTRICT

rationale: C3 is a GO sanctioning funds including a Rural Agriculture Market at Yedapalli; C2 gives operational guidelines for it, including tender and construction steps. This is an official step for one rural market, not yet operational, so in_progress.
No extract mentions railway privatisation or any state opposition to it. C1, C3 and C5 are about road over bridges built with Railways; C4 concerns metro rail funding.

cited.quote: mobile vegetable shops will be operated in five Corporations, viz, Chennai, Trichy, Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruppur

rationale: C2, a policy note, only states that mobile vegetable shops will be operated on a pilot basis. No GO or permit system for mobile marketing permits appears in any extract. Plans in a policy note are not operationalisation.

cited.quote: Taking up of widening works under the New Scheme
Widening and Improvement of State Highways, Major District Roads, Other District Roads

rationale: C1 gives in-principle approval for the road development programme (2021-11-17) and C3 gives administrative sanction (2021-12-16) for widening under CRIDP. These are official sanctions, but the extracts do not show completed 4/6-lane conversion, so in_progress.

cited.quote: All the essential commodities are supplied to the family cardholders using smart family cards in the Fair Price Shops.

rationale: C1 shows smart family cards were already in use before this government (all smart cards issued since 2017). No extract shows a new step to upgrade existing cards. C5 only promises smart cards to new applicants within fifteen days.

cited.quote: Fare structure which is in force from 29.01.2018 is presented below

rationale: C2 shows the bus fare structure in force is from 29.01.2018 and gives comparisons with other states. No extract shows a fare revision order. Concessions in C1 are not a revision of fares.
No extract mentions Varumun Kaapom Thittam or its restructuring. The extracts cover KNMT, Namakku Naame Thittam and AGAMT-II, which are different schemes.

cited.quote: Repair/reconstruction of 14,880 Houses in 149 old Samathuvapurams

rationale: C1 is G.O.(Ms) No.49 (2022-03-30) sanctioning funds and guidelines for repair and reconstruction of houses and infrastructure in 149 old Samathuvapurams. This is a dedicated measure for the scheme, which satisfies the directional commitment.

cited.quote: Jallikattu events are to be conducted only in those places that are notified in the State Gazette.

rationale: C1 and C2 discuss regulation of Jallikattu events. No extract shows any monthly assistance for people who raise Jallikattu bulls.
No extract concerns reviving English research centres. C1 and C2 are audit observations about idle university research centres, none relating to English.

cited.quote: In the first phase, this system has been implemented in 47 senior grade temples.

rationale: C1 reports the Annai Tamizhil Archanai system implemented in 47 senior grade temples with priests listed and Tamil archanai books launched 12.08.2021. Exact start date of the scheme is not stated, so only the year is given.

cited.quote: all the 4,57,645 petitions received under the programme have been acted upon.
On 08.05.2021, Hon’ble Chief Minister handed over the keys of the boxes containing the petitions

rationale: C2 says all 4,57,645 petitions were acted upon and the 100-day commitment implemented. C3 shows petitions handed to a Special Officer on 08.05.2021 and processed through the portal. Only about half were positively redressed, so some doubt remains.
No extract mentions a separate darshan queue for senior citizens in HR&CE temples. C1 and C3 describe department structure; C2 covers senior citizen tribunals.

cited.quote: These Elders Resource Centre functions as Day Care centres unlike shelter homes.

rationale: C3 shows Elders Resource Centres run on a pilot basis in two blocks per district as day care, not shelter. C1 shows old age homes run by NGOs. No official step creating centres with food, shelter and clothing at all district headquarters.

cited.quote: HIV counseling and testing services are provided through 2,962 centers located at various health care facilities

rationale: Extracts show only existing screening services (HIV testing in C2) and COVID surveillance in C3. No new order extending screening tests and diagnosis to all government hospitals.
